Mountain weather: read the forecast and prepare
What to do without mobile coverage

# Before departure
[ ] Choose a route suited to the group and daylight.
[ ] Download maps and check the return path.
[ ] Share your plan and return time with a trusted contact.
[ ] Pack navigation, light, shelter, clothing, food and water.
! A photograph or saved track does not confirm current trail safety.
# On the trail
- Reassess conditions and turn back early when needed.
Source: NPS Trip Planning Guide — https://www.nps.gov/articles/10essentials.htm

# Read more than the temperature
- Check precipitation, wind and storm risk before leaving.
- Consider the time of day, elevation and an early return option.
[ ] Carry layers and protection from rain and wind.
! Conditions can change. A forecast does not guarantee safe passage.
# If conditions deteriorate
- Avoid exposed ridges and water during storms; choose a safe retreat.
Source: NPS safety — https://www.nps.gov/yell/planyourvisit/safety.htm

# Packing checklist
[ ] Offline map, navigation skills and backup power.
[ ] Headlamp and spare power.
[ ] Weather protection and extra insulation.
[ ] First-aid supplies you know how to use.
[ ] Food, water and appropriate water treatment.
[ ] Emergency shelter.
! Fire equipment is not permission to light a campfire; follow local restrictions.
Source: NPS Ten Essentials — https://www.nps.gov/articles/10essentials.htm

# Prepare while connected
[ ] Download maps and share your itinerary.
[ ] Save your current coordinates and conserve battery.
# Without coverage
- Check your position against the offline map and known route.
- Do not take an unfamiliar shortcut just to search for reception.
! An offline map works without mobile data, but AreaMap cannot send an SOS message without a suitable connection.
- If lost, follow the existing lost-hiker guide and seek emergency help when a connection becomes available.

# Plan your supply
[ ] Carry water and suitable treatment supplies.
- Check reliable local information before relying on a natural source.
! Clear-looking water and photographs do not demonstrate drinking-water safety.
# Treatment
- Follow CDC guidance and the instructions for your treatment method. Boiling kills germs; filters vary and may not remove viruses.
- Treatment does not make chemically contaminated water safe.
Source: CDC — https://www.cdc.gov/drinking-water/prevention/water-treatment-hiking-camping-traveling.html

# Avoid an encounter
- Keep distance; do not feed or approach wildlife for a photograph.
- Store food and rubbish securely and follow local park instructions.
! The category photograph is illustrative, not evidence that this animal occurs on your route.
# If you see a bear
- Stay calm. Do not run or approach it. Give it space to leave.
- No single response works for every encounter; learn local species-specific guidance before your hike.
Source: NPS — https://www.nps.gov/subjects/bears/safety.htm

# Observe carefully
- Do not eat unfamiliar plants, berries or mushrooms.
- Do not pick plants in protected areas; photograph them instead.
! This photograph does not identify a poisonous or protected species. AreaMap does not provide plant identification from an image.
# Before the hike
[ ] Check local park rules and reliable regional identification resources.
- In case of suspected poisoning, seek professional emergency advice; do not use an unverified home remedy.
